{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|The transition to AAB is all about moving forward with technology. USI has served well, but its time has passed. AAB more than triples the data-flow which will allow advancements in sensory input, perhaps allowing advanced tactile functionality for droids and prosthetics in the near future.|[[Illia Setag]]|<ref name="Cybot Galactica Tries Proprietary Limbs">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|56|business/13516_2.html|Cybot Galactica Tries Proprietary Limbs}}</ref>}}
The '''Advanced Appendage Bus (AAB)''' was a proprietary universal socket interface utilized by [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]]<ref name="Advanced Appendage Bus (AAB)">{{CSWECite|I|12|Advanced Appendage Bus (AAB)}}</ref> to connect [[Limb/Legends|limbs]], heads and other appendages to a [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] [[Central processor/Legends|central processor]]. Its dataflow was more than triple that of the [[Universal Socket Interface]] standard, which would allow for advancements in sensory input, though only Cybot Galactica-manufactured parts were compatible with AAB sockets.<ref name="Cybot Galactica Tries Proprietary Limbs" /> Supporting software for the interface was developed at a Cybot Galactica-funded [[Cybot Galactica droid research institute|droid research institute]] located in the [[Financial District (Coruscant)/Legends|financial zone]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]].<ref name="Complete Locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> Some criticized the company's aggressive setting of a new standard,<ref name="Advanced Appendage Bus (AAB)" /> with competitors claiming that Cybot Galactica was attempting to its market share to cut smaller operations out of the lucrative droid replacement part business.<ref name="Cybot Galactica Tries Proprietary Limbs" />
